Our 3D Designer will give you the ability to choose your structure’s size, layout, colors, roofing type, and much more.     Use the 3D Designer to create the central section of your structure. This central structure is typically at least 3 feet taller than any lean-tos you plan to connect. Once you have your design completed, make sure to save it.

  2. Design Your Lean-tos

    Essentially, a lean-to is just a carport split in half. So, if you’d like an accurate price on a 12’ lean-to attachment on one side, you can separately price out a 24’ carport and divide that cost by half.

name: Metal Buildings Prices
description:
Metal building prices can range from $4,325 to $10,640 for a standard size steel building and $6,845 to $13,060 for a larger triple wide metal building, and over $20,000 for a commercial structure. In most cases, you can expect your steel building cost per square foot to land between $15 and $25.

However, these prices are subject to change at any time depending on several factors, including the dimensions of your building, the current price of raw steel, and the customization options you choose.
second_description:
Metal Building Price Ranges

Use this table as a quick starting point. Final cost depends on your exact dimensions, roof style, openings, and local code requirements.

Building Type Common Use Typical Price Range Notes
Standard Steel Building Storage, small shop $4,325 – $10,640 Pricing varies with size, roof style, and options.
Triple-Wide Metal Building 3-bay garage, workshop $6,845 – $13,060 Larger footprint + more openings can raise cost.
Commercial Steel Building Warehouse, business use $20,000+ Engineering and upgrades often increase totals.
Cost Per Square Foot Any building type $15 – $25 / sq. ft. A helpful range for early planning and budgeting.

What Impacts the Price of a Metal Building?

Two buildings with the same footprint can have very different price tags. Here are the biggest drivers we see when quoting projects at Top Goat Metal Structures.

1) Size, width, and height

Bigger buildings require more materials and may need additional structural support. In many cases, increasing length is more straightforward than increasing width, because wider clear spans often require more engineering and steel.

2) Wind & snow load requirements

Local codes can require higher wind ratings or heavier snow load capacity. Stronger requirements typically mean heavier framing and more reinforcement, which can increase the final price.

3) Open areas, lean-tos, and wall options

Open sides, partial enclosures, and attached lean-tos can change how wind loads apply to the structure. That can require upgraded engineering and materials compared to a fully enclosed design.

4) Customization & upgrades

Roll-up doors, walk-in doors, windows, insulation, taller legs, upgraded roof styles, and color options can all affect your quote. The right upgrades depend on your building’s purpose and climate.

5) Steel market conditions

Raw steel prices can move throughout the year. That’s why quotes can differ over time—especially when customers compare pricing from different months.
